record.paper_title: Open Questions in High Energy Spin Physics
record.original_question: Determine the physical origin and implications of the HERMES azimuthal asymmetry in semi-inclusive pion electroproduction from a longitudinally polarized proton target. In this setting, an observed pion azimuthal asymmetry could be a suppressed Collins-effect signal caused by the target spin's small component perpendicular to the virtual photon, or it could arise from twist-three helicity-flip effects suppressed by 1/Q. The open question is to distinguish these mechanisms and understand what the result implies for spin-dependent fragmentation measurements and access to transversity.

evidence.quote: What are the origins and implications of the Hermes azimuthal asymmetry?

This asymmetry could be a (suppressed) reflection of the Collins effect because the target spin, while parallel to the electron beam, has a small component, O(1/Q) perpendicular to the virtual photon. It could also result from competing twist-three helicity flip effects also suppressed by 1/Q.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider semi-inclusive deep-inelastic electroproduction of pions, $e\, p^{\uparrow} \to e'\, \pi\, X$, in which an unpolarized lepton beam scatters off a proton target whose spin is polarized along the lepton beam direction. Let $Q^2 = -q^2$ denote the (large) virtuality of the exchanged virtual photon, and let $\phi$ be the azimuthal angle of the produced pion measured around the virtual-photon direction relative to the lepton scattering plane. Define the single-spin azimuthal asymmetry $A_{UL}^{\sin\phi}(x, z, P_{h\perp})$ as the $\sin\phi$ moment (weighted by the target longitudinal polarization) of the normalized $\pi$ yield as a function of Bjorken $x$, the fragmentation variable $z$, and the pion transverse momentum $P_{h\perp}$.

Two distinct mechanisms can contribute to $A_{UL}^{\sin\phi}$ at order $1/Q$:

(i) A kinematically suppressed Collins-type contribution: because the target spin is aligned with the lepton beam rather than with the virtual photon, the target polarization has a transverse component (with respect to $\vec q$) of order $1/Q$, which couples the transversity distribution $h_1(x)$ of the proton to the Collins fragmentation function $H_1^{\perp}(z, p_\perp^2)$.

(ii) A genuine twist-three contribution, also suppressed by $1/Q$, involving helicity-flip quark–gluon correlations in the proton (e.g. the twist-3 distribution $h_L(x)$) convoluted with the Collins function, together with related twist-3 fragmentation pieces.

Problem. Develop a theoretical framework that cleanly separates contributions (i) and (ii) to $A_{UL}^{\sin\phi}$ (and to the related $\sin 2\phi$ moment) in pion electroproduction from a longitudinally polarized proton, and determine which mechanism dominates the observed asymmetry. Quantify the implications of the answer for:
 (a) the extraction of the Collins fragmentation function $H_1^{\perp}$ from spin-dependent fragmentation data, and
 (b) the feasibility of accessing the proton transversity distribution $h_1(x)$ via semi-inclusive measurements with longitudinally polarized targets, as opposed to transversely polarized targets.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent theoretical and experimental work (notably HERMES measurements with transversely polarized hydrogen targets and Collins-function fits including longitudinal-target data) has shown that the longitudinal-target azimuthal asymmetries can be largely understood as a combination of a kinematically suppressed Collins contribution (coupling transversity to the Collins function) and twist-3 pieces, with both contributions of comparable size. Direct, unambiguous separation of the two mechanisms purely from longitudinal-target data has not been achieved, but transverse-target measurements at HERMES and COMPASS have provided much cleaner access to the Collins function and transversity, partially resolving the original question.

status_evidence.title: Collins effect and single spin azimuthal asymmetries in the HERMES and COMPASS experiments
status_evidence.snippet: The overall normalization of the predicted asymmetries is fixed using information on the Collins fragmentation function extracted from previous HERMES data on azimuthal asymmetries from a longitudinally polarized target.
status_evidence.claim: Longitudinal-target HERMES asymmetries have been interpreted within a Collins-effect framework, supporting mechanism (i).

status_evidence.title: HERMES Measurements of Collins and Sivers Asymmetries from a Transversely Polarised Hydrogen Target
status_evidence.snippet: Measurement of Collins and Sivers asymmetries on a transversely polarised hydrogen target at HERMES.
status_evidence.claim: Transversely polarized HERMES data provided a cleaner extraction of the Collins function and transversity, partially resolving the original ambiguity.

status_evidence.title: On the cos φ_h asymmetry in electroproduction of pions in double longitudinally polarized process
status_evidence.snippet: Asymmetries in longitudinally polarized SIDIS include dynamical twist-3 contributions combining twist-3 TMD distribution/fragmentation with twist-2 partners.
status_evidence.claim: Twist-3 helicity-flip mechanisms remain an essential and active component of the theoretical description.
